synopsis: NIOSH Report of Investigations 9672 (Ruff, 2007) counted 22 fatalities involving blind areas using MSHA fatality reports from 2000 to mid-2006 [f3060]. Rear blind areas of reversing equipment accounted for 67% of victims; dump trucks had the highest share of fatal blind-area accidents at 38%, followed by front-end loaders at 33% [f3062, f3061]. The described accidents frequently involved large dump trucks driving over smaller vehicles or workers in blind spots [f3063]. The report also identified false alarms caused by a truck’s own tyres and protruding structures, connecting accident prevention to proximity-system reliability [f5435]. A vendor patent family citing the report makes the broader claim that false and nuisance alarms have traditionally been the primary reason deployed proximity systems fail; the supplied independent finding identifies specific alarm causes but does not establish that broader ranking [f10711, f5435].

relations.note: Specific false-alarm causes support, but do not establish, the vendor’s broader system-failure claim.
